newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - June regrade trades at -10cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - June regrade trades at -10cts.

text.p: Singapore June jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade traded in the negative for the first time for the prompt month as refiners lowered their jet offers in the face of poor demand, traders said on Monday.
"The regrade traded in the negative because of seasonal factors with the physical support not as strong as before," one trader said.
June regrade traded earlier in the day at minus 10 cents compared to the flat trade on Friday, brokers said. June was last quoted at between minus five and minus 15 cents, they said.
The front month regrade was valued at up to 60 cents earlier this month but had fallen sharply over the past few days as the physical support slowed down.
Early last week, deals were done at around the $25.00-per-barrel mark, free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis, but on Friday the buyers pulled to the sidelines in the wake of the selling onslaught.
On Friday, offers at between $24.75 to 24.90 per barrel failed to entice any buying interest with the last trade done at $25.15 on Tuesday.

Gas oil slipped slightly late afternoon from the morning with June swaps last quoted at $25.55/$25.65 per barrel, up 25 cents from Thursday, while July was indicated at $25.10/$25.20, also up 10 cents.
June swaps traded earlier in the day three times at $25.65 and at $25.70, brokers said.
Traders said the slide was in line with the weaker crude market after the big rise on Friday when July Brent ended 86 cents higher at $20.35 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
July Brent last traded down 19 cents to $20.16 per barrel.
Traders said the market remains well supported at current levels and the firmer crude prices might give some traders a fresh impetus to raise their physical bids.
On Friday, three 150,000-barrel cargoes traded, two at $25.20 and one at $25.70 per barrel, all on a free-on-board Singapore basis.
The $25.70 deal was the first time in about three weeks that physical gas oil traded above the $25.50 mark.
Fuel oil was steady with June quoted unchanged at $101/$102 per tonne.
